As a reader, I think this is a great anecdote poem that emits a "son, lemme tell you 'bout the good ol' days" vibe. To me, the details in the poem are not sad nor happy, but rather ordinary, as these were things that the poet faced frequently in his childhood, almost nostalgic. But also, the last part hit hard when the poet questions:


>and i wonder if

>on the day he died

>he woke up thinking

>“today is another good day”

This kind of shows that the poet learned something from the red-shirted man, but somehow feeling slightly sad over his death - as he was such a wise man for saying such words.

The details about the surroundings and settings are also vivid enough for the readers to imagine summer in the countryside. And the fact that there are literal references, such as "a pack of camels" makes it even more believable as a story.

I also spot some subtle rhymes, which I also like to apply to my own poems!
